evidence: US wholesale inflation slowed more than expected in July

nary_nodes.label: Producer Price Index Annual Increase (July)
evidence: The Producer Price Index, which tracks prices changes for producers and manufacturers, increased 4.7% in the 12 months that ended in July.

nary_nodes.label: PPI Annual Rate (June)
evidence: That was a slowdown from 5.5% in June, according to Bureau of Labor Statistics data released Thursday.

nary_nodes.label: Wholesale Inflation Cooling
evidence: Wholesale inflation is cooling off after the war in Iran caused a spike in oil and gas prices and other commodities.

nary_nodes.label: Producer-level Inflation Peak (May)
evidence: Producer-level inflation climbed to a four-year high of 5.9% in May before falling energy prices cooled things off a bit in June and July.

nary_nodes.label: Wholesale Food Prices Decline
evidence: Wholesale food prices also declined for the second month in a row.

nary_nodes.label: Core PPI Monthly Increase (July)
evidence: Core PPI, which excludes food and energy prices, rose 0.2% in July and slowed to 4.2%, the lowest rate in four months.

nary_nodes.label: Core PPI Annual Rate Slowdown (July)
evidence: Core PPI, which excludes food and energy prices, rose 0.2% in July and slowed to 4.2%, the lowest rate in four months.

nary_nodes.label: Consumer Price Index Cooling (July)
evidence: On Wednesday, the July Consumer Price Index showed that inflation of commonly purchased goods and services cooled for the second month in a row to an annual rate of 3.4%.

nary_nodes.label: Semiconductor Price Increase (Annual)
evidence: Semiconductor and other electronic component manufacturing prices, for example, are up 27.1% annually from a year ago, easing from the 27.7% annual rate notched in June.

nary_nodes.label: Price Hikes Could Slow for Consumers
evidence: Businesses’ costs aren’t rising as fast as they have been in recent months, an indication that price hikes could slow for consumers in the months ahead.

nary_nodes.label: PPI as Bellwether for Consumers
evidence: The PPI, a closely watched measure of wholesale inflation, serves as a potential bellwether for what consumers could experience in the near future; however, the higher prices businesses pay each other aren’t always fully passed on through the supply chain.

nary_nodes.label: Higher Prices Not Always Passed On
evidence: however, the higher prices businesses pay each other aren’t always fully passed on through the supply chain.

nary_nodes.label: War Caused Oil/Gas Spike
evidence: Wholesale inflation is cooling off after the war in Iran caused a spike in oil and gas prices and other commodities.

nary_nodes.label: Falling Energy Prices Cooled Inflation
evidence: before falling energy prices cooled things off a bit in June and July.

nary_nodes.label: Oil/Gas Prices Vary Widely
evidence: But since oil and gas prices can vary widely on a monthly basis and are subject to more on-time shocks – especially in the wake of a war – economists closely watch “core” inflation gauges that remove volatile components.

nary_nodes.label: Inflation Rising Faster Than Typical
evidence: Prices are still rising much faster than they typically do, however.

nary_nodes.label: Inflation's Negative Effect on Households
evidence: That’s been the case for more than five years now, and that’s had a compounding, negative effect on household finances and affordability.

nary_nodes.label: PPI Report May Portend Slower Inflation
evidence: The latest PPI report may portend slower inflation to end the summer, but fuel prices remain a wild card because of the ongoing Iran conflict, noted Ben Ayers, senior economist for Nationwide

nary_nodes.label: Fuel Prices Remain Wild Card
evidence: The latest PPI report may portend slower inflation to end the summer, but fuel prices remain a wild card because of the ongoing Iran conflict, noted Ben Ayers, senior economist for Nationwide

nary_nodes.label: AI Build-out Causes Localized Pressures
evidence: And while Thursday’s report paints a picture of a broader easing of wholesale inflation, it also highlights some more localized pressures resulting from the massive AI build-out and investment.

nary_nodes.label: AI Investment Diverts Production
evidence: The trillions of dollars being poured into AI-related components means storage and memory suppliers are prioritizing making the high-performance memory chips commanded by data centers.

nary_nodes.label: AI Investment Raises Costs
evidence: That’s diverted some of the production away from consumer products and raised costs for manufacturers.
